Implicit weights from a TWFE regression with covariates and staggered adoption

Source: R/twfeweights_mp.R
implicit_twfe_weights.Rd

Decomposes the coefficient on the treatment indicator from a two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regression with covariates, y ~ D + covariates | unit + time, into weighted comparisons between each treated group and the never-treated group in each time period (Caetano and Callaway, 2026). The weights within each comparison show how the regression reweights units, and twfe_cov_bal() reports how well they balance covariates.

Usage

implicit_twfe_weights(
  yname,
  tname,
  idname,
  gname,
  base_period = "first_period",
  xformula = NULL,
  data,
  weightsname = NULL
)

Arguments

yname

Name of the outcome variable.

tname

Name of the time period variable.

idname

Name of the unit identifier.

gname

Name of the group variable: the first period a unit is treated, or 0 for never-treated units.

base_period

Base period for each comparison: "first_period" (the default) or "gmin1" (the period before group \(g\) is first treated).

xformula

One-sided formula for the covariates in the TWFE regression, e.g. ~ x1 + x2. Time-varying covariates enter in levels, as in the regression. Default NULL (no covariates).

data

A panel data.frame in long format. Unbalanced panels are balanced first (with a warning about the rows dropped).

weightsname

Name of the column holding sampling weights, which must be constant over time within each unit. Default NULL (unweighted).

Value

An object of class decomposed_twfe: a list with

est

the TWFE coefficient on the treatment indicator.

decomposition_est

\(\sum w(g,t) \Delta(g,t)\), the estimate without the remainder terms.

decomposition_remainder

\(\sum w(g,t) r(g,t)\).

pt_violations_bias

the contribution of pre-treatment comparisons, \(\sum_{t < g} w(g,t) \Delta(g,t)\).

twfe_gt

a list with one element per \((g,t)\) cell holding g and tp (on a 1, 2, ..., T scale), alpha_weight, weighted_outcome_diff, remainder, the implicit weights for the treated and comparison units (weights_treated, weights_comparison) and the comparison group's effective sample size ess.

idname, tname, gname, weightsname, data

inputs, kept for twfe_cov_bal().

Details

For each treated group \(g\) and period \(t\) (including pre-treatment periods), the function computes a weighted average of the change in outcomes from a base period for group \(g\) minus the same for the never-treated group, with weights coming from the residual of a regression of the (double-demeaned) treatment on the (double-demeaned) covariates. The TWFE coefficient is $$\alpha = \sum_{g,t} w(g,t) \big[ \Delta(g,t) + r(g,t) \big],$$ where \(w(g,t)\) is alpha_weight, \(\Delta(g,t)\) is weighted_outcome_diff and \(r(g,t)\) is remainder in each element of twfe_gt. Weights on post-treatment cells sum to one. Pre-treatment comparisons also enter the estimate; their contribution is reported as pt_violations_bias. With base_period = "first_period" the remainders are zero; with base_period = "gmin1" each comparison uses period \(g-1\) as the base period, like did::att_gt(), and the remainder terms are typically small.

Covariates with collinear (double-demeaned) values are dropped; for example, time-invariant covariates drop out unless interacted with time, as in ~ x + as.factor(year) * as.factor(region). Without covariates (xformula = ~1) and with base_period = "gmin1", each comparison equals \(ATT(g,t)\) from did::att_gt() (universal base period) and alpha_weight equals the weights from twfe_weights().

References

Caetano, Carolina and Brantly Callaway. "Difference-in-Differences when Parallel Trends Holds Conditional on Covariates." Working paper (2026). doi:10.48550/arXiv.2406.15288

See also

twfe_cov_bal(), summary.decomposed_twfe(), implicit_aipw_weights(), two_period_reg_weights() for two periods.

Examples

data(castle, package = "causaldata")
castle <- as.data.frame(castle)
castle$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post")

tw <- implicit_twfe_weights(
  yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",
  xformula = ~ l_police + unemployrt, base_period = "gmin1", data = castle
)
